$comment: DOKIPON commerce — LOCAL DEVELOPMENT fixture set. Every credential in this file is a local development value, published on purpose so a local run is reproducible and deterministic. None of them is a credential. The services refuse to start while a published development value is in place (services/crates/commerce-core/src/secrets.rs); a local run is the legitimate case for that guard, so `switch` below sets DOKIPON_ALLOW_DEV_SECRETS=1. A deployment must never read this file.

switch.why: The guard in commerce-core/src/secrets.rs refuses the published development values (dev-only-admin, dev-only-key, dev-channel, dev-only-secret, dev-only-service-token) unless this switch is set. A local run sets it. A deployment must not.

credentials.$comment: The values below are local-only names, NOT the published development values, so this file cannot be mistaken for a deployment's credential set. `env` is the variable name the service reads.

lineIdTokenKey.readBy: commerce-identity, and mock-line-identity (it signs with this key)

lineChannelId.readBy: commerce-identity (the id_token's audience), and mock-line-identity (it mints for this channel)

serviceToken.readBy: commerce-order (the operator's view of the orders), and commerce-admin (presents it)

ports.$comment: The services read PORT one per process; the launcher sets it from this map. The mock ports are the crates' own defaults (services/crates/commerce-mocks/src/bin/*.rs) and are overridable with PORT as well.

seed.$comment: The services seed themselves. This fixture set POINTS at those seeds; it does not duplicate them — a second copy of a catalogue is a second truth. Every service reads the same seeds in every topology (services/crates/commerce-edge/src/stores.rs builds them for the in-process edge and the function topology alike).

catalogue.contents: 10 products, each with one SKU. 7 of the SKUs are Reserved (they carry a stock level), 1 is MadeToOrder (sku-cami-01), 2 are Unbounded (sku-beauty-01, sku-goods-01). p-adult-01 is web-only: it is not eligible for the app or the LINE channel.

expected.note: GET /v1/products answers 10 items for the web channel and 9 for channel=app and channel=line (p-adult-01 is eligible for web only). The channel filter is the server's job, not the client's (services/crates/commerce-catalog/src/lib.rs:285).

inventory.contents: The 7 Reserved SKUs of the catalogue, with the same quantities. A SKU in the catalogue but not in the ledger makes a purchasable product fail at the last step of checkout, so the two lists must stay identical.

expected.note: The ledger holds no level for the MadeToOrder and Unbounded SKUs: those do not take part in the inventory step.

content.contents: The content document is NOT seeded: it starts EMPTY (revision 0, every section at its default) unless CONTENT_PATH points at a JSON document that already exists. The service persists what the operator writes back to that path, atomically.

expected.note: A local run that wants a persisted document sets CONTENT_PATH to a writable path and PUTs /v1/content with the expected revision; a run that does not set it keeps the document in memory only.

cartAndOrders.contents: Both start empty. A local run creates a guest session (POST /v1/sessions/guest) before it can put anything in a cart.

mockAgreement.$comment: The mock issues LINE-shaped id_tokens and the identity service verifies them. If the two disagree about the token's shape, every test that uses the mock is testing a fiction. This test mints with the mock and verifies with the product's own verifier, using the credentials above on both sides.
